questions.name: persona
questions.instructions: Which group best describes the role in `connection.current_position`?

questions.name: seniority
questions.instructions: How senior is the role in `connection.current_position`?
criteria: A student, intern, or someone not currently working in a professional role
An individual contributor who does the work and does not manage people or a budget
A manager or team lead who runs a team and influences what that team buys
A director, head of department or vice president who owns the budget for their function
A founder, owner, partner or C-level executive who makes final buying decisions

questions.name: role_fit
questions.instructions: How closely does the role in `connection.current_position` match the buyers described in `ideal_customer.target_roles`, given what is sold in `ideal_customer.what_we_sell`?
criteria: The role has nothing to do with the target roles or with the problem the product solves
The role sits in a neighbouring function and would only hear about the problem second-hand
The role works inside the target function and deals with the problem day to day
The role is one of the target roles and would own the decision to solve the problem

questions.name: company_fit
questions.instructions: Judging from `connection.current_company` and, if given, `connection.company_description`, does the company match `ideal_customer.target_companies`?

criteria.fits: The company is recognisably the kind of company described as a target
criteria.does_not_fit: The company is recognisably outside the target, or matches `ideal_customer.not_a_fit`
criteria.cannot_tell: The information given does not reveal what the company does or how big it is

questions.name: likely_buyer
questions.instructions: Would the person in this role plausibly take part in deciding whether to buy what is described in `ideal_customer.what_we_sell`?

criteria.true: They own, approve or strongly influence this kind of purchase
criteria.false: They would not be involved in this kind of purchase, or they match `ideal_customer.not_a_fit`

recipes.note: When previous is present, the 02 questions (change_type, new_budget_owner, current_role_buys; CHANGE_QUESTION_VERSION 2) are added to the same call, with `connection` in place of `current`.

scoring.fit_0_100: round(100 * sum(w_i*part_i)/sum(w_i)); parts: role_fit=score/3, seniority=score/4, likely_buyer=noul, company_fit=P(fits)

questions.name: change_type
questions.instructions: Compare the role in `previous` with the role in `current`. What kind of change is this?

criteria.moved_up: A step up in seniority, scope or responsibility
criteria.moved_sideways: A different job at a similar level of seniority
criteria.same_job_reworded: The same job and employer written differently, such as an abbreviation being spelled out or a team name added
criteria.moved_down_or_unclear: A step down, a gap in employment, or not enough information to say

questions.name: new_budget_owner
questions.instructions: Does the role in `current` own a budget for `what_we_sell` that the role in `previous` did not?

criteria.true: The new role runs the function that would buy this, and the old role did not
criteria.false: Buying power for this is unchanged, lower, or was already there before

questions.name: current_role_buys
questions.instructions: Is the role in `current` one whose holder decides whether to buy `what_we_sell`?

criteria.true: They run sales, revenue, growth or the whole company, so they would own this decision
criteria.false: Their function does not buy this, even if the role is senior

questions.name: intent
questions.instructions: What is the sender of `reply` telling us, in response to the cold email in `our_email`?

criteria.interested: Wants to talk, asks for a meeting, times or more information
criteria.not_now: Open to it but explicitly later, or asks to be contacted again at a future time
criteria.referral: Points us to a different person who handles this
criteria.objection: Engages but pushes back on price, fit, timing or an existing vendor
criteria.not_interested: Declines without asking to be removed
criteria.out_of_office: An automatic away or out-of-office message
criteria.unsubscribe: Asks to stop receiving emails or to be removed

questions.name: wants_removal
questions.instructions: Does `reply` ask, in any wording, to stop being contacted or to be removed from the list?

criteria.true: Any request to stop, remove, unsubscribe or not be contacted again

questions.name: names_another_person
questions.instructions: Does `reply` name or point to a different person we should contact instead?

questions.name: route
questions.instructions: Given the form submission in `lead` and the routing rules in `routing_policy`, where should this lead go?

criteria.account_executive: A qualified buyer with a real, near-term need
criteria.sdr_qualify: Possibly a buyer, but the need, authority or timing is unclear
criteria.nurture: Early research or a small company that is not ready to buy
criteria.partner_or_vendor: Someone trying to sell to us, partner with us, or recruit
criteria.junk: Spam, a test, a student, or nonsense

questions.name: urgency
questions.instructions: How soon does the person in `lead` need a solution, based on what they wrote?
criteria: No need stated, or just browsing
Exploring options with no timeline
Planning to act this quarter
Needs something now, with a deadline or a pain happening today

questions.name: is_vendor_pitch
questions.instructions: Is the person in `lead` trying to sell something to us rather than buy from us?

questions.name: intent
questions.instructions: What does the sender of `invitation_message` want from us?

criteria.pitching_us: Wants to sell us a product or service
criteria.potential_buyer: Describes a problem that `what_we_sell` solves, or asks about our services
criteria.peer_or_community: Same industry, shared group or event, wants to connect as a peer
criteria.recruiting_or_job: Hiring, or looking for a job
criteria.unclear: Too short or generic to tell

questions.name: worth_a_reply
questions.instructions: Given `what_we_sell`, is `invitation_message` worth a personal reply?

criteria.true: A potential buyer, a warm intro or a relevant peer
criteria.false: A pitch, spam, or nothing to respond to

questions.name: sells_b2b
questions.instructions: How clearly does `company.description` show that this company sells to other businesses?
criteria: Sells only to consumers, or the description says nothing about customers
Mostly consumers, with some business customers
Sells to both businesses and consumers
Sells mainly or only to businesses

questions.name: needs_outbound
questions.instructions: How much does the business in `company.description` depend on a sales team reaching new customers directly?
criteria: Customers find and buy on their own, such as self-serve apps or retail
Mostly inbound or partner-led, with a small sales team
A sales team closes deals, but most leads come in by themselves
Growth depends on salespeople contacting buyers who did not ask first

questions.name: size_fit
questions.instructions: Using `company.employees`, where does this company fall relative to `target_size`?

questions.name: excluded
questions.instructions: Does the company in `company` match any of the exclusions in `exclusions`?

questions.name: building_outbound
questions.instructions: Does `job_post` show the company is building or rebuilding a team whose job is to contact prospective customers directly?

criteria.true: Hiring SDRs, BDRs, outbound AEs, or a leader to build that team
criteria.false: Any other kind of hire, including account management for existing customers

questions.name: first_hire_in_function
questions.instructions: Does `job_post` suggest this is one of the first hires in this function at the company?

questions.name: seniority_of_hire
questions.instructions: What level is the role in `job_post`?

questions.name: supported
questions.instructions: Do the facts that `first_line` relies on appear in `source`? Ignore greetings and well-wishes; judge only the factual claim.

criteria.supported: The source states or clearly implies the claim
criteria.contradicted: The source says something that conflicts with the claim
criteria.unsupported: The source does not mention it; the claim may be invented

questions.name: sounds_creepy
questions.instructions: Does `first_line` bring up the recipient's private life?

criteria.true: Mentions health, illness, family members, children, relationships, religion or other personal matters, even if the person shared them publicly
criteria.false: Refers only to their job, company, industry or professional achievements

questions.name: about_them
questions.instructions: How much is `message` about `prospect` and their situation, rather than about the sender?
criteria: Entirely about the sender, their product or their company
Mostly about the sender, with a generic nod to the prospect's industry or role
Refers to something specific about the prospect, but most of the message is the pitch
Built around something specific to the prospect, with the offer secondary

questions.name: pitches_first_line
questions.instructions: Does the first sentence of `message` pitch a product, service or meeting?

questions.name: reads_as_template
questions.instructions: Would `prospect` recognise `message` as a mass template sent to many people?

criteria.true: Generic flattery, merge-field phrasing, or lines that could be sent to anyone
criteria.false: Could only have been written to this person

questions.name: clear_ask
questions.instructions: Does `message` end with one clear, low-effort question or request?

questions.name: about_them
questions.instructions: How much is `opener` about the recipient and their situation, rather than about the sender?
criteria: Entirely about the sender, their product or their company
Mostly about the sender, with a generic nod to the recipient's industry or role
Refers to something specific about the recipient, but most of the message is the pitch
Built around something specific to the recipient, with the offer secondary

questions.name: pitches_first_line
questions.instructions: Does the first sentence of `opener` pitch a product, service or meeting?

questions.name: asks_a_question
questions.instructions: Does `opener` ask the recipient a genuine question about their situation?

questions.name: references_a_trigger
questions.instructions: Does `opener` mention a specific recent event about the recipient, such as a new role, a post, a hire or a launch?

questions.name: buying_interest
questions.instructions: At any point in `thread`, did the other person show interest in buying, evaluating or learning about what `me` offers?

criteria.true: Asked about pricing, services, a call, or described a problem we solve
criteria.false: Networking, small talk, hiring, or a pitch to us

questions.name: who_owes_reply
questions.instructions: Looking at the last message in `thread`, who should reply next?

criteria.me: The other person asked something or is waiting on us
criteria.them: We asked something and are waiting on them
criteria.nobody: The conversation reached a natural end

questions.name: topic
questions.instructions: What is `thread` mainly about?

criteria.sales_conversation: A possible deal for what `me` offers
criteria.networking: Getting to know each other, intros, events
criteria.pitch_to_me: The other person selling to us

questions.name: path_to_buyer
questions.instructions: At the company in `target_account`, how is the person in `connection` related to the buyer described in `target_account.buyer`?

criteria.is_the_buyer: Their role is the buyer role, or one that owns this decision
criteria.leads_the_buyer: Senior to the buyer, such as a founder, CEO or the executive the buyer reports to
criteria.same_team: Works in the buyer's function, below or beside them
criteria.other_team: Works elsewhere in the company and would have to find the buyer
criteria.unclear: The title does not say enough

questions.name: intro_strength
questions.instructions: How well placed is the person in `connection` to introduce us to the buyer in `target_account.buyer`?
criteria: Works in an unrelated part of the company and likely does not know the buyer
Works nearby and may know the buyer by name
Works with the buyer regularly and could make a warm introduction
Is the buyer, or directly manages them, so no introduction is needed

questions.name: action
questions.instructions: Given `what_we_sell`, what should we do about `post`?

criteria.engage: The author describes a specific problem of their own, happening now, that we solve
criteria.monitor: About our market or a debate on the topic, but the author states no problem of their own
criteria.ignore: Unrelated, a tutorial, a job post, or someone promoting their own product

questions.name: author_is_buyer
questions.instructions: Does `post` suggest its author would be the one to buy `what_we_sell`?

questions.name: self_promotion
questions.instructions: Is `post` mainly promoting the author's own product, service or content?

questions.name: next_step
questions.instructions: Given `thread`, which of our follow-ups in `templates` should we send next, or should we stop?

criteria.bump: They have not replied yet and it has been a few days; a short nudge fits
criteria.case_study: They showed mild interest or asked how it works; proof would help
criteria.breakup: Several follow-ups got no reply; a final polite close fits
criteria.answer_manually: They asked a specific question that a template cannot answer
criteria.stop: They declined, asked to stop, or the conversation is over
